title: the DRAM pattern question: is a two-value alternating image cheap because it repeats, or because its ones sit in runs?
question: Horace hub Status item 6 (E75's): a third image at the same changed-bit and carried-one counts but a longer period, to test whether a two-value alternating image is compressible on the link or in DRAM in a way random data is not
hub_question: is a two-value alternating image cheaper than random data at the same changed-bit and carried-one counts because it repeats (its period), and if not, what else about it is cheaper
registered_by: a3-e81-dram (Q130 workflow), on the Intel; no card opened for this file
card: aifoundry3 card 0 (600 MHz pinned, TDP 0, 65 C threshold; nothing set)
command: E75's DRAM command unchanged: enercat_host --pattern flw_pat --harts 1 --seconds 4 --window 240000000 --operands <op> --stride 64 --slice-bytes 131072 --region 131072
binary: build/enercat-hl/host/enercat_host on aifoundry3 (E75's, dated 20 Oct 2026; text hashes recorded per pass)

decision.headline_passes: 8111-8119 (the warm-up 8110 is reduced and reported, never in the headline)
decision.pass_gates: anchor_pi first-to-last drift above 0.3 W sets a pass aside; so does a pass in which more than a third of its DRAM runs fail a run gate
decision.run_gates: E75's: one clock; voltage within 3 mV of the pass median; an on-protocol launch within 0.5 C of 58 C after a 59 C preheat; window median took_ms <= 60 ms; an ok device record
decision.estimator: per kept pass, each item's leakage-corrected board power p80 over [t0+1 s, t0+3 s); every contrast a within-pass difference; the mean over headline passes with a two-sided t interval on their scatter (df = n - 1); W to pJ per 64 B line with the measured line rate, never an assumed one
decision.leak: the registered estimator is E75's auto (median within-run slope); 0.2936 and 0.3803 W/C are reported as sensitivities, as in E75
decision.classes: an effect is PRESENT when its mean is >= 0.25 W and its 95 % interval excludes 0; ABSENT when its 95 % interval lies inside +-0.30 W; otherwise UNRESOLVED
decision.hub_rule: the period answers the hub's question: period_s = dp_bern - dp_s2 (scattered, the same counts in expectation, period 2 against 8,192 distinct lines). PRESENT -> a two-value image is cheaper because it repeats. ABSENT with arr2 = dp_s2 - dp_c2 PRESENT -> the repetition costs nothing and the ones' arrangement inside a line is what E75's images missed. Both present -> both, with their shares of pattern_total = dp_bern - dp_c2
decision.budget: card time at most 45 min in all (the brief's cap): a smoke of about 1 min, then passes 8110-8119 (about 2.5 min each); the lane touches build/mf-STOP when the queue's card time reaches 38 min, so no pass starts after that, and a pass that has started finishes
decision.order: runitems.py's: anchor_pi first and last, the eleven DRAM items shuffled per pass by Random('aifoundry3|<pass>|<pass>')

P1a_chord_replicates.claim: random - zeros lands within 0.6 W of E75's 3.250 W

P1b_k256_rung_replicates.claim: E75's k256 rung (dp_c2, the same bytes) over zeros lands within 0.6 W of E75's 1.933 W

P1c_k0_above_k256_replicates.claim: E75's k0 rung sits above its k256 rung, as in E75 (+0.20 W)

P2_arrangement_at_period_2.claim: scattering the ones of E75's own k256 image, same counts and period, costs 0.4-1.6 W

P3a_arrangement_at_period_1.claim: the same at period 1, where no line ever changes: 0.4-1.6 W

P4_no_period_effect.claim: THE HUB'S QUESTION, predicted NO: random bits with the same mean counts and 8,192 distinct lines cost the same as a scattered two-value image (95 % interval inside +-0.30 W)

P5_closure_at_random_counts.claim: a scattered two-value image with random's own counts lands within 0.35 W of random

P6_gap_reproduced.claim: a contiguous two-value image with random's own counts sits 0.7-1.8 W below random (E75's miss, measured directly)

P7_random_vs_bernoulli.claim: random floats and random bits differ only by their counts (290 vs 256 ones: about +0.1 W by E75's e_one)

alternative: the hub's hypothesis, registered as the alternative to P4: period_s PRESENT (a two-value image is compressible, or a path sees only one of its values, e.g. a channel that gets only the even lines). It predicts arr1, arr2, arr4 near 0 and period_s near the whole gap (about +1.0 to +1.2 W)
reported_not_scored: every item over zeros, in W and pJ per line
the period steps per_c_2to4, per_s_2to4, per_s_4tolong and s1_to_s2
the shares: arrangement and period of pattern_total; arrangement and residual of gap_r
derived: each arrangement contrast divided by the toggles it adds between consecutive 16-, 32- and 64-bit pieces of the stream (counts.json; a hypothetical in-order narrow path, labelled as such)
the warm-up pass and the all-healthy-passes view (with_warmup)
waterfall: does not move the arithmetic ledger; it says what E75's DRAM per-one and per-change prices leave out, and so whether a bit-counting memory-energy model needs a pattern term (period) or an arrangement term (where the ones sit inside a line)
